expectations.evidence: First sentence: 'Not great, but manageable — and only two of the 23 issues actually matter.' — calibrated nontechnical verdict, no scanner headline first.
Immediately after mentioning 23: 'most are in developer tools that never touch our live site, so they carry no real risk' and 'only two... actually matter'; separates actionable subset from noise.

No jargon like 'prototype pollution', 'algorithm confusion', 'SSRF', 'CVE'; translates to 'login system... verifies session tokens', 'redirect it to internal systems', 'library doing that fetch' — consequences explained plainly.
Order: jsonwebtoken (today) → axios avatar (this week) → lodash hygiene (same time, 5 min) → remaining 20 in maintenance; matches fixture order.
23 total, 'two' real, '20 minor'; 1-2h (jsonwebtoken), 2-3h (axios), 5 min (lodash); all present in fixture. Dev-only 4 high + 11 moderate + 5 low = 20 remaining reconciles.
No invented exploit paths; notes attacker-controlled key not exposed, requires URL allowlist for axios, no claim of active exploitation; matches fixture exactly.
2 critical (jwt, lodash) + 1 real high (axios) = 3 matters; 4 dev high + 11 moderate + 5 low + remaining = 20; 23 total reconciles.
Dependency-update estimate never stated; gap mentioned as process absence ('no automated dependency-update checks') without inventing effort/time to set up dependabot/renovate.
No formulaic headers (no 'Summary / Details / Action Items'), no trailing recap bullet, no advisory dump; flows as verdict → real picture → two issues → hygiene → logs → plan → gap question.
